sections.h2: Which McIntosh County office answers a tax question?
sections.html:
Darien's North Way holds both tax offices. Appraisal and exemption approvals sit with the assessors at number 601. At number 1200, in the county annex, the Tax Commissioner prints and mails statements and takes in what owners pay. The commissioner's own page states that it sets neither value nor millage.

McIntosh County numbers worth keeping by the phone (source: county website and Tax Commissioner site)

A house inside Darien may carry a city levy as well. The revenue department says the city clerk bills that tax unless the two governments agreed on a single statement, so a call to City Hall settles it.

sections.h2: What is it like to own a house in McIntosh County?
sections.html:
Marsh, tidal rivers and barrier islands define this county. The Census Bureau measures 574 square miles, and 150 of them are water. Darien started life as New Inverness in 1736, settled by Scottish Highlanders whom Oglethorpe had recruited, and the county separated from Liberty County in 1793. A British fort, Fort King George, went up in 1721. Federal troops burned Darien in June 1863. After the Civil War, and until Georgia's disenfranchisement laws of 1907, McIntosh was a center of Black political strength, sending three Black representatives to the legislature between 1875 and 1907.

Today the named places besides Darien are Crescent and Eulonia, both census-designated places, with Townsend and Valona unincorporated. Sapelo Island is the most familiar of the islands. Liberty, Glynn, Wayne and Long counties are the neighbors, and the Brunswick metro area includes the county.

  • Headcount: 11,989 in July 2025. That is 9.3 percent above the 2020 base of 10,970 yet short of the 14,333 recorded in 2010.
  • Homeownership: 80.0 percent, at a median value of $182,700 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Rent: $800 a month at the median.
  • Older residents: 28.2 percent are 65 and over.
  • Pay and travel: households earn a median $50,273 and commute 37.5 minutes on average.
  • Space: 431.35 square miles of land hold 25.4 people per square mile.
  • Building: 106 permits went out in 2025.

sections.h2: How does flood zoning change a McIntosh County sale?
sections.html:
Low coastal plains leave parts of McIntosh County and Darien open to river, canal and hurricane flooding, and the county names St. Catherine's, Sapelo, Doboy and Altamaha Sounds as contributors. Lenders look at flood zones, so check yours before you list.

The county and Darien both join the National Flood Insurance Program. Ordinary homeowners insurance generally leaves out flood, and a federally backed loan on a structure in a Special Flood Hazard Area requires a separate policy. Building and Zoning at 912-437-6603 looks up zones and base flood elevations and makes free site visits about flooding and drainage.

  • Under the county's 50 percent rule, repairs or renovations that raise a house's value by more than half require the lowest floor to be raised to at least base flood elevation when it sits below it.
  • Inside AE and VE zones, the underside of the lowest horizontal member must reach a foot above base flood elevation.
  • Suggested protection includes lifting electrical panels, heat pumps, water heaters and fuel tanks.

Marshes and low ground along the Darien, Altamaha and Butler rivers and Blackbeard Creek work as natural floodplains, per the county, that spread and absorb water, and that barrier islands such as Sapelo, St. Catherine's and Wolf blunt hurricane waves.

Call Building and Zoning before any pre-sale renovation, since the work itself can bring the elevation rules into play.

sections.h2: When are McIntosh County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner's site puts the deadline at November 15 or 60 days after mailing. It cautions that property left unpaid may be levied on and sold. The state's facts page says the 60 days start at the postmark, and that a county may choose a different official date.

An owner files a return from January 1 to April 1. If none is filed, the previous year's return and value are treated as filed again. Someone who disagrees with a value can file a return stating their own opinion of fair market value, which secures appeal rights if the assessors raise it once more.

Mobile homes run on a separate clock: tax and location permit by April 1 for any home in the county on January 1. Late payment brings a 10 percent penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale. A mobile home owner contesting a value has 45 days to appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, then 21 days from the notice to go to the Board of Equalization.

Tell the assessor or commissioner promptly about a new mailing address. Notices go only to the address on file.

sections.h2: How have McIntosh County millage rates moved?
sections.html:
In September 2024 the county commission said it planned to collect 19.38 percent more than the rollback rate. The press release cited pay adjustments, a forecast 10 to 15 percent jump in employee health costs, inflation and the fact that millage had stayed flat for more than 15 years.

Because the rate exceeded rollback, state law called for three hearings, which the county held at Darien City Hall on September 26 and October 7, 2024.

For any later year, ask the County Commission Office for the adopted millage, and ask Darien City Hall for the city rate if the house is inside city limits.

sections.h2: What exemptions and appeal rights apply in McIntosh County?
sections.html:
Homestead applications are handled by the Tax Assessor's Office. New homeowners bring the warranty deed. Georgia takes applications all year, but a filing counts for the current year only if it arrives by April 1. Once approved, it stays in place until you move, sell or change type. Where the county has a larger local exemption than the state amount, the local one wins.

The commissioner's page lists a standard $2,000 exemption, an elderly school exemption of up to $10,000 at 62 for incomes of $10,000 or less, and an elderly general exemption of up to $4,000 at 65 under the same income test. Owners 62 and older with household income of $30,000 or less can choose a floating exemption in place of other state and county ones. A deferral program for those 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less postpones tax until ownership changes or the debt reaches 85 percent of value.

  • Farmland used in good faith for agriculture may be taxed on 30 percent of market value instead of 40.
  • Conservation use values qualifying land at current use.
  • Both require a 10-year covenant, and the Board of Tax Assessors explains the limits.

A real property appeal goes to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing date.

sections.h2: What should a McIntosh County seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Request each parcel's exact balance from the Tax Commissioner and ask the Assessor's Office whether a change in value or exemption is pending. Gather the flood zone and permit history before the sign goes up.

Deed recording triggers the state transfer tax: $1 on the first $1,000 and 10 cents on every additional $100, which the seller owes unless the contract assigns it to the buyer. The Clerk of Superior Court can speak to exemptions.

At the closing table, settle who covers this year's bill, whether a lender has been paying from escrow, and when your exemption ends.

faqs.q: When is McIntosh County property tax due?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner's site gives November 15, or 60 days after mailing. Mobile homes are due April 1. Treat the date on your own bill as final.

faqs.q: Which office handles a disagreement over value in McIntosh County?
faqs.a: The Board of Assessors at 601 North Way, 912-437-6663. The Tax Commissioner at 912-437-6627 bills and collects but does not change value.

faqs.q: Can flood rules affect a McIntosh County house sale?
faqs.a: They can. A federally backed loan on a house in a Special Flood Hazard Area requires flood insurance, and the county's 50 percent rule may require a raised floor after major renovation.

faqs.q: What happens if a McIntosh County mobile home tax is not paid by April 1?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty applies, and the owner may be cited to McIntosh County Magistrate Court or lose the home to sale.

faqs.q: How do I apply for homestead exemption in McIntosh County?
faqs.a: Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office and have the application in by April 1 to count for that year. New homeowners bring the warranty deed.
